annotations.text:
Code — the first category done properly

Today every question is a prompt string and a textarea, whatever the subject. That is fine for "why does a stoma close" and useless for "where is the off-by-one".

This canvas takes one category all the way down: what a code question is made of, the three screens the learner actually sees, the shapes the database and the prompts need, and the four packages that make it render.

Static mockups, matching the existing learnos canvas — not a clickable prototype.

Deliberately not designed here

Maths and system design were in the original ask and are not on this canvas. They need their own renderers (KaTeX, React Flow) and their own prompt fragment, and designing three categories at once is how you end up with a block union that fits none of them.

The structure above is built to take them: a new domains/*.md file, new block kinds in the same union, the same three slots. Nothing on the session screen changes when they land.

The rule this bumps into

loop.md §2: "UI: plain React, inline styles or a single styles.css — no UI library for the pilot."

The stack on the left keeps three of four packages on the backend precisely to stay inside that. CodeMirror does not: it is a UI library, on the client, on one screen.

That is a founder call, not a call a task should make quietly. Written up as T-081 rather than assumed.
